raw.assessment: The incumbent delivered every ordered design and catches fitting problems before dispatch. Rework affected five of eight large, two of fourteen medium, and none of eighteen small covers, supporting investigation of size-dependent dimensional error without establishing its cause. Small unadjusted covers demonstrate 25–31-minute production is possible, but preventing seven reworks alone does not establish a batch median below 32 minutes. The concrete limiting observation is that both observed customer placement failures involved rounded corners absent from reference tables: passing the current check may not establish customer fit. Wash-length variation and unmeasured width changes leave dimensional stability unresolved; the weight-based waste estimate does not verify the area limit.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: sewing and measuring one cover per size before committing the remaining cuts can reveal repeatable dimensional errors early enough to correct cutting allowances within the existing stock.
openings.delta: Replace whole-batch cutting with staged dimensional feedback; distinguish repeatable allowance error from variable sewing error.
openings.prediction: Repeatable allowance error produces consistent finished-dimension deviations for a size; variable seam execution produces deviations that change between comparable covers.
openings.probe: Record ordered, cut and sewn dimensions, seam uptake, design, cutting direction, operator and stage times for initial covers; check subsequent same-size covers before generalizing. Measure retained samples in both axes through the stipulated wash test. Recalculate cutting waste by area before altering layouts.
assumptions: Initial covers remain deliverable; any correction must pass wash, design, area-waste, budget and deadline constraints.
Small pilot results require confirmation across affected sizes and cloth conditions.

openings.claim: Do rounded corners cause placement failure independently of errors in nominal tabletop dimensions?
openings.delta: Separate corner-shape mismatch from overall size mismatch that reference-table testing could conceal.
openings.prediction: Shape-specific mismatch remains at matched actual length and width; dimension mismatch instead tracks discrepancies between actual and ordered measurements.
openings.probe: Request actual length, width, thickness and corner measurements from willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare placement observations across measured tables, locating pocket interference versus general tightness or slack.
assumptions: Without suitably matched tables, shape and size effects remain confounded.

raw.assessment: Geometry mismatch and cloth response are plausible, unconfirmed causes. Neither opening establishes the batch targets; interaction benefits require comparison against each mechanism alone.

openings.claim: Cross customer geometry measurement with staged first-article sewing at an order-specific cutting-and-corner-pocket card. Measurements define the intended shape; sewing feedback calibrates how that shape translates into finished dimensions before remaining matching pieces are cut.
openings.delta: Geometry cards alone can repeat an incorrect sewing allowance; staged checks alone can optimize for the wrong reference-table geometry. Their combination could prevent both errors from propagating.
openings.prediction: The combination reduces first-placement adjustment more than either component alone, particularly where measured geometry differs from nominal dimensions. Unchanged failures despite verified geometry would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Prioritize the four nominal-dimension orders within the six available customer measurements, recording corner shape as well as length and width. Compare geometry-only, staged-calibration-only, and combined corner assemblies using retained offcuts. Validate selected settings on sellable first articles; record actual customer placement separately from reference-table fit.
assumptions: Enough comparable assemblies exist for a meaningful comparison.
Changes honor ordered size/design and pass wash/removal checks within 350 units, three weeks, and 8% area waste.

openings.claim: Cross two-axis wash measurements with layout selection at the compensated panel dimensions supplied to the cutting marker. A layout is eligible only when its cloth direction and measured shrinkage jointly yield acceptable finished geometry.
openings.delta: Shrinkage compensation alone can require wasteful panel dimensions; layout optimization alone can choose a direction with unsuitable shrinkage. Joint selection could retain fit while meeting the area-waste ceiling.
openings.prediction: If directional shrinkage matters, jointly selected layouts outperform uncompensated layouts after five washes and use less area than compensation with a fixed layout.
openings.probe: Track length and width through five washes on identifiable offcuts. Compare fixed-layout compensation, layout-only selection, and joint candidates on paper before cutting. Reject candidates exceeding 8% measured area waste or changing visible design orientation; time the added work.
assumptions: Design permits at least two layout choices.
Measured variation is repeatable; total cost and median working time remain within limits.

openings.claim: Stage sewing before remaining cuts to expose dimensional error.
openings.discriminator: Repeatable size deviations versus variable seam execution.
openings.probe: Log order/cut/sewn dimensions, seam uptake, design, direction, operator and stage times; confirm across same-size covers; use D4 wash evidence.
openings.uncertainty: Pilot generalization and time savings unproved.

openings.claim: Separate corner mismatch from nominal-dimension error.
openings.discriminator: Corner interference at matched actual dimensions versus general tightness/slack.
openings.probe: Collect length, width, thickness and corners from willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders; compare placements.
openings.uncertainty: Unmatched tables confound shape and size; observation access uncertain.

openings.claim: Combine measured geometry and staged calibration in order-specific cutting/pocket cards.
openings.discriminator: Combined benefit exceeds either component alone.
openings.probe: Prioritize four nominal-only orders within six measurements; compare geometry-only, calibration-only and combined offcut assemblies, then sellable articles; distinguish customer placement from reference fit.
openings.uncertainty: Measurement fidelity and comparable assemblies unresolved.

openings.claim: Jointly select directional shrinkage compensation and layouts.
openings.discriminator: Better washed fit than uncompensated layouts; less waste than fixed-layout compensation.
openings.probe: Measure identifiable offcuts in both axes through five washes; compare fixed compensation, layout-only and joint layouts on paper; measure area waste and added time.
openings.uncertainty: Representativeness, repeatability and multiple permissible layouts unknown.

post_distill.decision: Probe before committing cuts. Require ordered sizes/designs, purchased stock, <=8% area waste, five-cycle wash survival, tool-free removal, two machines, <=350 units and three weeks. Weight-based waste is insufficient. No target established: verify >=38/40 first placements, all designs and median <=32 minutes.
